item.title: More Candidates — No Hit@20 Increase: An Experiment Analysis
item.description:
In my recommendation system, items from subsequent registered purchases were more frequently lost before ranking. I increased candidate quotas from descriptions and images: the overall limit grew from 300 to 370. Then, I recalculated features and retrained LightGBM on the same data. For 625 sessions with a registered target, candidate coverage increased from 66.24% to 68.96%, but hits in the top 20 dropped from 389 to 388. This article details the loss analysis, experiment conditions, and the decision to retain the original setup without claiming statistical superiority. The project uses Coveo data. Code and reproduction instructions are open-source. Let's analyze the experiment.

item.title: AI Agent Took the Wheel of My Pet Project. I'm Taking It Back With Interactive Explanations and Two Prompts
item.description:
Hi everyone! My name is Dina, I'm a Java developer with about six years of enterprise experience. Since April, I've been working on a pet project with an AI agent: it wrote the code, I set tasks and watched the tests. Everything was going well: tests were green, scenarios were closed, and then I opened the project and realized I didn't clearly understand how the main scenario worked: from request to finished video. This article is about how I regained understanding of my own code. Read more

item.description:

item.title: 5 Tasks I No Longer Want to Do Manually After Discovering AI Agents
item.description:
If I do the same boring operation manually for the second time, an AI agent somewhere in the world gets sad. And if it's the third time, it's probably already a Python script. Lately, I've found myself increasingly reluctant to manually parse Excel, convert documents, write one-off utilities, or deal with yet another terminal error. Not because I've forgotten how. It's just that many of these tasks can now be delegated to an AI agent, which can not only suggest a solution but also execute it. I've gathered five everyday scenarios where AI agents genuinely save me time. No fantasies about replacing entire professions – just practical examples, limitations, and a bit of pain from manual work. Read more

item.title: What part of the internet still belongs to people?
item.description:
Content production is getting cheaper. Even from a free neural network, you can get an illustration, a composition with the right mood, or even a book in seconds. But what are the scales of the problem? Have we reached the era of the generated internet, or not yet? Since we don't have a registry of everything on the internet, it's impossible to determine the share of human content. However, I managed to find studies on the share of generations in news, books, photos, and music. I suggest we discuss them. Spoiler: almost all segments show a kind of overproduction, which I recently mentioned in the context of scientific papers: it's much easier to create content than to check, edit, or advertise it. Disclaimer: academic research lags behind the development of models and people's habits of using them. Therefore, when providing a figure, I indicate the moment (and based on what analysis) it was calculated. Keep in mind that the situation has changed since 2025, and there haven't been many new studies since then. Also, for each study, one can make a reservation that researchers do not have reliable data on the share of AI; they use detectors, which are usually the same AI, just "on the side of good." Read more

item.title: How I Made AI Agents Gather Their Own Harness for a Specific Task
item.description:
I gave Claude Code (Opus 5.5) a test assignment: to draw a scene from Blade Runner 2049 in SVG. The agents I tried all failed similarly: they didn't look at the actual frame, drew from memory, and reported completion mindlessly. So, I started prompting the agent with questions: is there documentation, what should the result be compared against, when should it stop? These questions evolved into AutoHarness – a skill that forces the agent to prepare for a task before starting it. Read more
